deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivation. It continues Gauss's 'A collection of knots', the English-language list begun on the previous page (headed 'J.F.E. Gauss. 1794'). The previous page has items 1-8: thumb knot, loop knot, draw knot, ring knot, running knot, and an unnamed knot with ends a, b, c, d that closes or opens depending on which pair of ends is pulled. This page continues the numbering.

(9) 'fishers knot or water knot': described as knot 4 (the ring knot) 'twice drawn through the ring'. A word after '4,' is struck out.
(10) 'meshing knot': a drawing of two strands interlaced in a sheet-bend / netting-knot configuration. Two ends leave upward and two leave downward.
(11) 'barbers knot': 'is the same but the two upper ends laid across'. It is defined as a variant of (10), obtained by crossing the two upper ends.
(12) 'bowline knot': a drawing of a fixed loop with a standing part and a tucked working end, the standard bowline.
(13) 'a wale knot' (wall knot): named but not drawn.

Below the list Gauss adds two bibliographic notes in German and Latin. First: 'Andere sind gezeichnet bei Riedl, Beiträge zur Theorie der Seh(n)enwinkel(?), Wien 1827, 8°', meaning other knots are drawn in Riedl's book, octavo, Vienna 1827. Second, in pencil: 'C. J. 's Gravesande, Philosophiae Newtonianae [Institutiones / Elementa] II. 45', a reference to 's Gravesande's Newtonian physics textbook, volume II, item 45. That book discusses ropes, friction and knots in its mechanics sections.

The 1827 reference shows the page was annotated well after the 1794 date of the list. The next page lists permutations and partitions of four letters a, b, c, d. That is plausibly an attempt to enumerate ways of pairing or ordering four rope ends, connecting to knot 8 with ends a-d. This connection is my inference.

No mathematical computation is performed on this page. It is a descriptive catalogue of practical knots with literature references.
errors: No mathematical errors, because no mathematics is carried out.

The descriptions are informal. 'Fisher's knot = ring knot twice drawn through the ring' is a loose description: the usual fisherman's knot is two overhand knots, each tied around the other strand. The equation with knot 4 depends on what Gauss's 'ring knot' denotes.
Calling the netting/meshing knot 'the same' as a barber's knot with the upper ends crossed is a practical description, not a precise topological identification.

results.what: Catalogue of practical knots (fisherman's/water knot, meshing knot, barber's knot, bowline, wall knot) with drawings, continuing the 1794 list 'A collection of knots'
results.modern_name: Descriptive catalogue of practical (seamanship) knots; prehistory of knot theory
results.usually_credited_to: Traditional seamanship literature. Gauss's knot sheets in Math. 33 are discussed by M. Epple (1998-1999) as early evidence of his interest in knots, leading later to the linking-number integral of 1833.

results.what: Literature references for knot drawings: Riedl (Vienna 1827) and 's Gravesande, Philosophiae Newtonianae Institutiones II.45

deep.surprise_reason: This is a known page from Gauss's early knot collection, dated 1794 on the preceding sheet. Historians, notably Epple, have already described and published on these knot sheets. The page contains only names and drawings of practical knots plus references, with no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: There are 24 orderings of four rope ends a,b,c,d. This is context for the permutation list on the next page, which writes out those beginning with a and b (12 of them).
There are 3 ways to split four ends a,b,c,d into two unordered pairs (ab|cd, ac|bd, ad|bc). The next page lists 6 because it treats the two pairs as ordered.

transcription_corrections: 'Andrea [?] sind gezeichnet bei [?]' should read 'Andere sind gezeichnet bei' (i.e. 'Others are drawn in').
'Riedl Beiträge zur Theorie der Sehnen-winkel' is uncertain. The handwriting looks like 'Schnen-' or 'Sehnen-winkel', and the exact title should be checked against Riedl, Vienna 1827.
'Wien 1827. 8.' means octavo format ('8°'), not a page or volume number.

'C. J. s' Gravesande' is 'G. J. 's Gravesande' (Willem Jacob 's Gravesande), written in pencil. 'Philosophiae Newtonianae' refers to his 'Physices elementa mathematica ... sive Introductio ad philosophiam Newtonianam'.
Line 2: the struck-out word after '4,' is illegible. The sense is 'like no. 4, twice drawn through the ring'.
'wale knot' is Gauss's spelling of 'wall knot'.
